decisions.title: Electrocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Reduction Coupled with Alcohol Oxidation
decisions.evidenceBasis: Compact handoff title/source metadata identify an electrocatalytic paired CO2-reduction/alcohol-oxidation study; no abstract or affirmative evidence establishes a general preparative organic-synthesis method or substrate-scope contribution.
decisions.challengeReason: Challenge considered whether paired alcohol oxidation could qualify as synthetic electrosynthesis; absent evidence of a general preparative organic product method, the protocol requires exclusion rather than inference from an organic half-reaction.

decisions.title: Disentangling Electronic and Lattice Contributions to Transient Absorption in Metal Halide Perovskites: A First-Principles Study of CH3NH3PbBr3
decisions.evidenceBasis: Compact handoff abstract is a first-principles transient-absorption study of a metal-halide perovskite and contains no preparative organic synthesis method.
decisions.challengeReason: No substrate scope, bond-forming synthetic protocol, total synthesis or polymerization methodology is present; this is computational/materials photophysics.

decisions.title: Enantioselective Defluorinative C(sp2)–H Allylation of Acrylamides Enabled by CpxRh(III) Catalysis
decisions.evidenceBasis: Compact handoff abstract reports a convergent CpxRh(III)-catalyzed enantioselective olefin–olefin cross-coupling of acrylamides and allylic difluorides, broad structural diversity, up to 99% yield/99% ee, and divergent access to chiral 2-piperidones.
decisions.challengeReason: The central contribution is a general preparative asymmetric C–H functionalization/defluorinative coupling method with substrate scope and synthetic products; no exclusion criterion applies.

decisions.title: Non-Canonical Peptide Self-Assembly for Mitochondria-Specific Cargo Delivery
decisions.evidenceBasis: Compact handoff abstract centers on peptide self-assembly, mitochondrial cargo delivery and antitumor immune effects rather than a general organic synthesis method.
decisions.challengeReason: Although a defined tetrapeptide/conjugate is prepared, synthesis is enabling material for a biomedical delivery study and is not the methodological contribution.

decisions.title: Isoindole-Based Multicomponent Synthesis of Pyrimido[6,1,2-cd]pyrrolizine Fluorophores with Unsymmetrical Urea Handles: Photophysical, Theoretical, and Antifungal Imaging Studies
decisions.evidenceBasis: Compact handoff abstract explicitly reports a diversity-oriented one-pot multicomponent synthetic strategy generating a library of PP fluorophores with unsymmetrical urea functionality from readily accessible precursors.
decisions.challengeReason: Despite downstream photophysical and antifungal-imaging studies, the paper contains an explicit library-generating multicomponent preparative method; the synthetic methodology is substantive rather than incidental.

decisions.title: All the ways a cell can die — and why the variety matters
decisions.evidenceBasis: Nature d41586 identifier and title identify a news/feature article about modes of cell death; compact handoff contains no synthetic-method abstract or preparative chemistry evidence.
decisions.challengeReason: No general organic synthesis method, total synthesis, substrate scope or polymerization methodology is indicated; the subject is cell biology/news rather than synthetic chemistry.

decisions.title: Hundreds of ‘free’ academic journals have started charging fees
decisions.evidenceBasis: Nature d41586 identifier and title identify a news/reporting article about journal fees, not chemical research.
decisions.challengeReason: No synthetic chemistry method, preparative scope, total synthesis or polymerization methodology exists.

decisions.title: Direct C1–H Amination of Free NH Carbazoles Enabled by the Catellani Reaction
decisions.evidenceBasis: Compact handoff abstract reports the first Pd/NBE-catalyzed C1–H amination of unprotected carbazoles, broad cyclic-amine scope and functional-group tolerance, providing concise access to C1-aminated scaffolds.
decisions.challengeReason: The central contribution is unequivocally a general preparative C–H amination methodology with scope; no exclusion criterion applies.
